To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the flow properties of the maternal blood are altered in pregnancies complicated by maternal hypertension.

the flow properties of the maternal blood are a determining factor in placental perfusion, that these properties change during pregnancy in parallel with changes in the hematocrit and that these changes are more pronounced in hypertensive pregnancies.

(a) WBV is increased in hypertensive pregnancy; (b) the higher WBV values are related to a higher incidence of fetal complications; and (c) WBV is a useful tool in the management of pregnancy complications.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a new approach to the pathogenesis of pregnancy hypertension.
the relationship of hemorheology to the development of pregnancy-induced hypertension and to its complications.
the relationship of maternal blood viscosity to pregnancy hypertension and its complications.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
maternal whole blood viscosity is a determining factor, which contributes to fetal and maternal morbidity in pregnancy hypertension, but that it is not the only one.
WBV is an independent risk factor for fetal complications, but not for maternal complications.
WBV is not a determining factor in maternal complications, whereas it is a determining factor of fetal outcome.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the maternal blood flow is impaired in pregnancy hypertension, and that this impairment is reflected in an increase of whole blood viscosity.
WBV is an important parameter in the prediction of fetal and maternal outcome.

maternal whole blood viscosity is an important determinant of the efficacy of placenta perfusion, and that the increase in whole blood viscosity during pregnancy is a prominent feature of preeclampsic pregnancies.
The main takeaway from our work is that
WBV can be used to predict fetal outcomes in pregnancy hypertension, independently of the severity of blood pressure elevation.
maternal whole blood viscosity is an important determinant of placental perfusability and, consequently, of fetal outcome.
the viscosity of blood is an important factor that affects blood flow.
